earlier_scan.source_named: No grammar or phonology located for Baelelea; Glottolog page shows no descriptive references.

sources.citation: OLAC. Resources in and about the Baelelea language (ISO 639-3 bvc). Internet Archive copy 2024 of language-archives.org/language/bvc.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: 'Language descriptions' lists only the Glottolog stub. Primary texts are PARADISEC audio only: Capell AC1-433 'Malaita Island (north and south), Guadalcanal Island' (1970) and Ian Frazer's IF01 cassette series 1973-74. No SIL, no thesis, no dictionary entry for bvc.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: bvc/Baelelea occurs only in the ISO-639-3 code table; no stress record for the language.

sources.citation: Lichtenberk, Frantisek. 2008. A Grammar of Toqabaqita (Mouton Grammar Library 42). Berlin: Mouton de Gruyter. ch. 1.1 p.1 and sect. 2.3 Stress pp.19-27.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Baelelea appears only on p.1 as a co-'dialect' of Tryon & Hackman's North Malaitan and in one lexical note (noni 'body' also in Baelelea per T&H 1983). The stress rules of sect. 2.3 are stated for Toqabaqita alone; no claim is made about Baelelea.

sources.citation: Lichtenberk, Frantisek. 2008. A Dictionary of Toqabaqita (Solomon Islands). Pacific Linguistics 592. Introduction pp.1, 9.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: p.1: Toqabaqita, Baeguu, Baelelea, Fataleka and Lau 'are considered to be different languages' by speakers though T&H treat them as North Malaitan dialects; p.9: 'With some exceptions stress is predictable' -- Toqabaqita only, nothing about Baelelea.

sources.citation: Siegel, Jeff. 1986. Wai: a Malaitan language in Fiji. In Geraghty, Carrington & Wurm (eds), FOCAL II, 435-463. Pacific Linguistics C-94.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Names Baelelea among the mutually intelligible North Malaitan varieties (p.442) and consulted one Baelelea speaker, Manuel Maesua (note 15, p.459); sec. 3.2 'Wai phonology' (pp.447-448) covers segments and vowel length of Wai, the Fiji koine, only. Nothing on stress for Wai or Baelelea.

sources.citation: Tryon, Darrell T. & B. D. Hackman. 1983. Solomon Islands languages: an internal classification. Pacific Linguistics C-72. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Mbaelelea is wordlist no. 65 (Ma) and a 'major dialect or sublanguage' of North Malaitan with To'ambaita, Mbaengguu, Fataleka (p.27; Lau kept separate 'for reasons of tradition', p.27 fn.1). Wordlists and sound-correspondence tables only; a full-text search for stress/accent/penult finds no statement about stress in any language.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3. Languoid page Baelelea (bael1237). Hammarström, Forkel, Haspelmath & Bank (eds).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only two references attached: Tryon & Hackman 1983 (overview/wordlist) and Siegel 1986 (overview); no grammar, sketch, phonology or dictionary; AES 6a vigorous. Nothing on stress.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: One sentence plus an Ethnologue 18 citation; no linguistic content.

sources.citation: Ethnologue (Eberhard, Simons & Fennig, eds). Baelelea entry [bvc], 'Language Development' and 'Writing' fields.

sources.note: Would confirm whether any literacy/orthography materials (e.g., SITAG/Wycliffe scripture portions, alphabet books) exist for Baelelea that might carry a note on stress; page is subscription/could not be reached by automated download.

sources.citation: Lichtenberk, Frantisek. 1988. The Cristobal-Malaitan subgroup of Southeast Solomonic. Oceanic Linguistics 27(1-2): 24-62.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: publisher DOI, paywalled; library e-access not checked
sources.note: Comparative paper that uses Baelelea data (index lists Baelelea pp.26, 31-35, 37, 38, 43-45); could be checked for any phonological note on stress in the North Malaita varieties, though comparative papers of this kind rarely give one. Archive.org copy is access-restricted.

sources.citation: Simons, Gary F. 1980. Malaitan pronouns / Solomon Islands language survey materials (as cited by Siegel 1986: 'Simons 1980:3' on speaker numbers and mutual intelligibility of North Malaitan varieties).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Siegel's source for the Malaitan language inventory; a survey that might include orthographic or phonological notes on Baelelea. Exact title and access not verified here.

sources.citation: Ross, Harold M. 1973. Baegu: social and ecological organization in Malaita, Solomon Islands. Illinois Studies in Anthropology 8. Urbana: University of Illinois Press. Appendix A 'Baegu Phonology', p.293.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Nearest full-page phonology of a variety Ross himself (p.49) groups with Baelelea as dialects of one language; gives penultimate accent for Baegu. Would let the catalog record a sister-dialect statement with an explicit identity caveat; full page not readable (archive.org lending item).

sources.citation: Capell, Arthur (compiler/recorder). 1970. Malaita Island (north and south), Guadalcanal Island. PARADISEC collection AC1, item AC1-433 (audio; Baelelea listed among content languages). Report on Arthur Capell Estate by Peter Newton (1995), AC1-000.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only archived primary material tagged bvc on OLAC; Capell's north-Malaita wordlist recordings could be used to hear stress placement, and any accompanying field notes might contain a remark on accent. Not a published statement.

sources.access_detail: only an abstract or snippet reachable
sources.note: Hits are Wikipedia PDF dumps, the T&H 1983 scan, Ross 1973 Baegu (p.49 lists Baelelea as a dialect of the Lau-To'abaita-Baegu group), Keesing's Kwaio dictionary, ethnographies, OL 27 (1988) subgrouping paper, Hollyman 1960 checklist, and Global Recordings Network 78 rpm 'Jonah' / 'Who is He?' in Baelelea (audio). No description of Baelelea; no snippet mentions Baelelea stress.
